1: # SwapDesk
2: 
3: SwapDesk arranges shoe exchanges for a fictional shop. A customer asks for a different size, and the system checks policy and stock, holds a replacement, creates a return and a mock label, then verifies the saved state. Every request ends in one of four outcomes: **exchange arranged**, **clarification required**, **policy denial**, or **human escalation**.
4: 
5: All data is synthetic. There are no payments, shipments, or real customers. This is a neatHack project built by a team of four.
6: 
7: ## Repository layout
8: 
9: ```text
10: frontend/          Next.js dashboard — standalone client-side demo (no backend required)
11: src/swapdesk/      Python backend package — FastAPI, SQLite, LangGraph agent
12: eval/              Frozen benchmark, deterministic checker, and run harness
13: tests/             Deterministic pytest suite (no network, no model)
14: docs/              Build plan, runbooks, evidence, and business deliverables
15: hackathon.md       Incremental build log and team conventions
16: pyproject.toml     Python dependencies (uv) — FastAPI, LangGraph, neatlogs
17: langgraph.json    LangGraph Studio wiring (offline + live assistants)
18: opencode.json      MCP servers (cfo.ai, neatlogs) and agent configuration
19: .env.example       Key names only — copy to .env, never commit secrets
20: ```
21: 
22: ## The two halves
23: 
24: - **Backend** (`src/swapdesk/`) — the agent runtime. Policy checks, atomic stock reservation, idempotent operations, an append-only action journal, a LangGraph tool-using agent, and a FastAPI surface for frontend integration. Deterministic and network-free to test.
25: - **Frontend** (`frontend/`) — the ops dashboard (Mission Control, Inbox, Inventory, Integrations, Customer Simulation, ticket detail). It is a **self-contained client-side demo** powered by a mock store — it demos the SwapDesk experience without calling the live API. Its own README lives at [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md).
26: 
27: ---
28: 
29: ## What was planned
30: 
31: The build ran in order: tool setup and a test commit, then the mock shop and checker before the agent, then a first working version with a measured baseline. After that came injected failures, trace reading, fixes, and a re-run for before-and-after numbers, followed by the business plan, a demo screen, and repo cleanup, ending with the video. Full spec in [`docs/build-plan.md`](docs/build-plan.md) — a plan, not evidence of what happened. What actually happened lives in [`hackathon.md`](hackathon.md).
32: 
33: ---
34: 
35: ## Backend
36: 
37: ### Features
38: 
39: - Atomic stock reservation with no oversell, safe under concurrent writers.
40: - Idempotent operations: same key plus same payload returns the saved result; same key plus different payload is rejected.
41: - Policy enforcement: delivered status, 30-day return window, final-sale excluded.
42: - One active exchange per order item, across cases.
43: - Append-only action journal for every committed or duplicate-routed operation.
44: - Full mock exchange lifecycle: reserve → return → label → arrange, plus hold release, cancel, escalation, cleanup recovery, and a read-only verification handoff.
45: - Demo-only failure injection (`faults.py`) with same-key recovery.
46: - A LangGraph tool-using agent (`langchain.agents.create_agent`, Gemini or a LiteLLM proxy): curated tools, bounded loop, budget-capped requests, file-backed checkpoints, database-derived outcomes, template replies.
47: - neatlogs wiring (workflow/tool spans, local capture without a key, export with one).
48: 
49: ### Installation
50: 
51: Requires Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
52: 
53: ```bash
54: git clone https://github.com/adr1en360/SwapDesk.git
55: cd SwapDesk
56: uv sync
57: ```
58: 
59: ### Test
60: 
61: ```bash
62: uv run pytest -q
63: ```
64: 
65: The suite is deterministic — no network, no model keys, no LLM judge.
66: 
67: ### Run the API
68: 
69: ```bash
70: uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app
71: ```
72: 
73: Interactive docs at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` (generated from the implementation, always in sync). The demo database is `swapdesk.db` (override with `SWAPDESK_DB`); restarting reuses it, fixtures seed once.
74: 
75: | Method & route | What it does |
76: |---|---|
77: | `POST /v1/tickets` | Submit a ticket and run it to a verified outcome (201) |
78: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}` | Verified status, outcome, reply, run ids (404 unknown) |
79: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline` | Sanitized action/journal events (404 unknown) |
80: | `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue` | Continue with message/consent (404 unknown, 422 uncontinuable) |
81: | `GET /v1/fixtures` | Synthetic orders, items, and policy for dropdowns |
82: | `POST /v1/demo/faults` | Demo-only: arm one failure on an operation key |
83: | `DELETE /v1/demo/faults` | Demo-only: disarm all failures |
84: | `GET /v1/health` | Liveness probe |
85: 
86: Outcomes (`arranged`, `clarification`, `denial`, `escalation`) always return 200 with an `outcome` field — a denial is an answer, not an error. Only malformed requests (422), unknown cases (404), and unexpected failures (500, generic message) are HTTP errors.
87: 
88: ```bash
89: curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/tickets \
90:   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
91:   -d '{"order_id":"ORD-1001","order_item_id":"ITEM-01","size":"42"}'
92: 
93: curl localhost:8000/v1/cases/CASE-xxx
94: curl localhost:8000/v1/cases/CASE-xxx/timeline
95: curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/cases/CASE-xxx/continue \
96:   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
97:   -d '{"consent_size":"42","order_id":"ORD-1005","order_item_id":"ITEM-06","size":"43"}'
98: ```
99: 
100: No authentication: this is a local mock. Execution runs synchronously per request, so status reads are never blocked.
101: 
102: ### Configuring the agent
103: 
104: Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in what you have (`.env` is git-ignored; never commit it):
105: 
106: - `GEMINI_API_KEY` — direct Gemini access (no `LITELLM_API_KEY`).
107: - `LITELLM_API_KEY` — enables the hackathon LiteLLM proxy instead; `SWAPDESK_MODEL` then picks from `nova-micro`, `nova-lite`, `nova-pro`, `nova-2-lite`, `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-4.6` (default `claude-haiku`). Override the endpoint with `LITELLM_BASE_URL`.
108: - `SWAPDESK_MODEL` — Gemini model id when using Gemini directly (default `gemini-3.8-flash`).
109: - `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` + `NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID` — neatlogs telemetry export; local-only capture works without them.
110: 
111: Live model calls and telemetry export need working egress to the upstream APIs; where the network blocks them, the deterministic suites still pass.
112: 
113: ### Inspecting the agent in LangGraph Studio
114: 
115: Two graphs share one architecture (`prepare` → nested `agent` subgraph → `verify`), defined in `src/swapdesk/agent/studio_flow.py` and served from `langgraph.json`:
116: 
117: ```bash
118: uv run langgraph dev
119: ```
120: 
121: Open Studio at `https://smith.langchain.com/studio/?baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:8123`. Two assistants are registered:
122: 
123: - **`swapdesk_offline` (default).** A scripted model replays tool calls against the real backend — zero model requests. Proves the wiring, never Gemini's decisions.
124: - **`swapdesk_live` (opt-in).** Budget-capped Gemini. Needs `SWAPDESK_MODEL` plus `GEMINI_API_KEY` (or the LiteLLM pair) and a per-run budget; anything missing fails loudly before any model call.
125: 
126: Full runbook with evidence: [`docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md).
127: 
128: ## Frontend
129: 
130: A Next.js 16 (Turbopack) App Router dashboard with React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS v4.
131: 
132: ### Run it
133: 
134: ```bash
135: cd frontend
136: npm install
137: npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000
138: ```
139: 
140: Other scripts: `npm run build` (production build), `npm run start`, `npm run lint`.
141: 
142: ### Pages and demo flow
143: 
144: | Route | Page | What it demos |
145: |---|---|---|
146: | `/` | Mission Control | Agent metrics + live execution queue |
147: | `/inbox` | Inbox | Sample ticket stream |
148: | `/inventory` | Inventory | Stock levels that react to simulations |
149: | `/database` | Database Schema | Tables the agent reads/writes |
150: | `/integrations` | Integrations | Inbound webhook triggers (Zendesk, Shopify, Gorgias) |
151: | `/settings` | Agent Settings | Autonomy/guardrail config UI |
152: | `/simulate` | Customer Simulation | Inject a customer complaint into the queue |
153: | `/ticket/[id]` | Ticket Execution | Per-ticket action timeline |
154: 
155: The demo runs entirely on a client-side store (`frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx`). **Simulate Ticket** prepends a resolved ticket and decrements `AJ4-MIL-43` stock; **Customer Simulation** injects a ticket with an `Agent Processing` status; **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) restores the initial state. Dashboard labels reflect the actual mock state — completion rate is computed from the queue, and cost shows "Demo Mode".
156: 
157: SEO is configured across all routes (per-page metadata, generated Open Graph/Twitter images, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`). See [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md) and [`frontend/setup.md`](frontend/setup.md) for details.
158: 
159: ## Evaluation and evidence
160: 
161: - `eval/cases_v1.json` — frozen 30-case benchmark (`benchmark-v1`, 8 holdouts) covering arrangement, denial, clarification, and escalation, with seeded fault schedules.
162: - `eval/driver.py` — deterministic reference driver (not the agent) that exercises the cases.
163: - `eval/harness.py` + `eval/run.py` — isolated database per run; results committed to `eval/results/v1.json`.
164: - `src/swapdesk/checker.py` — deterministic per-outcome checks and global invariants, no LLM judge.
165: - `docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md` — a controlled live BEFORE/AFTER comparison of the D1 final-sale denial evidence path.
166: 
167: ## Documentation
168: 
169: | Doc | Purpose |
170: |---|---|
171: | [`docs/build-plan.md`](docs/build-plan.md) | Full build plan (spec, not evidence) |
172: | [`docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md) | LangGraph Studio runbook with evidence |
173: | [`docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md`](docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md) | Runner/harness evidence walk-through |
174: | [`docs/business/`](docs/business/) | Business plan (MD/PDF) and financial model (XLSX) — figures are assumptions, not observed facts |
175: | [`hackathon.md`](hackathon.md) | Incremental build log and conventions |
176: 
177: ## Contributing
178: 
179: - Backend owns `src/swapdesk/` and `tests/`. Frontend owns `frontend/`.
180: - Keep tests deterministic; business logic stays callable without HTTP or a model.
181: - Record each change in `hackathon.md` with the exact commands run and pass/fail counts.
182: - Never commit `.env`, databases, or real customer data. `.env.example` carries key names only.
183:

<content>
1: # SwapDesk Frontend
2: 
3: The frontend dashboard for **SwapDesk** — autonomous middleware between a e-commerce helpdesk and its commerce stack that resolves exchanges, returns, and refunds safely. It is an idempotent, policy-aware agent runtime.
4: 
5: Built as a self-contained Next.js app with **client-side demo state** — no backend is required to run or demo it.
6: 
7: ## Tech Stack
8: 
9: - **Next.js 16.4.0** (App Router, Turbopack, `cacheComponents` + `partialPrefetching` enabled)
10: - **React 19** with Server & Client Components
11: - **TypeScript** (strict), path alias `@/*` → `./src/*`
12: - **Tailwind CSS v4** (CSS-first theme tokens in `app/globals.css`)
13: - **lucide-react** icons
14: - **sonner** toasts
15: - Fonts via `next/font/google`: **Bricolage Grotesque** (display), **Plus Jakarta Sans** (body), **Geist Mono** (technical/mono)
16: 
17: ## Getting Started
18: 
19: ```bash
20: npm install      # install dependencies
21: npm run dev      # start the development server (http://localhost:3000)
22: ```
23: 
24: Other scripts:
25: 
26: | Script          | Description                                    |
27: | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
28: | `npm run build` | Production build (static + partial prerender)  |
29: | `npm run start` | Serve the production build                     |
30: | `npm run lint`  | ESLint (flat config)                           |
31: 
32: ## Environment Variables
33: 
34: | Variable                 | Default                             | Purpose                                                                |
35: | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
36: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`   | `https://swapdesk.vercel.app`       | Canonical origin used for `metadataBase`, canonical URLs, sitemap, robots. Override when deploying. |
37: 
38: ## Project Structure
39: 
40: ```
41: app/
42: ├── layout.tsx              # Root layout, global <head> metadata, fonts, SwapDeskProvider, Toaster
43: ├── page.tsx                # Server entry → renders <MissionControl />
44: ├── mission-control.tsx     # "Mission Control" home (client) — metrics + live queue
45: ├── inbox/page.tsx          # Full ticket inbox (static demo data)
46: ├── inventory/              # Live stock + reservations (client; stock reacts to simulations)
47: │   ├── layout.tsx          #   metadata
48: │   └── page.tsx
49: ├── database/layout.tsx     # Schema view (metadata)
50: ├── integrations/           # Inbound webhook triggers (Zendesk, Shopify Inbox, Gorgias)
51: │   ├── layout.tsx          #   metadata
52: │   └── page.tsx
53: ├── settings/layout.tsx     # Agent autonomy/guardrail settings (metadata)
54: ├── simulate/page.tsx       # Customer Simulation — inject a ticket into the queue
55: ├── ticket/[id]/page.tsx    # Ticket execution detail (Suspense split; see below)
56: ├── robots.ts               # /robots.txt
57: ├── sitemap.ts              # /sitemap.xml
58: ├── opengraph-image.tsx     # Generated OG image (ImageResponse)
59: ├── twitter-image.tsx       # Re-exports from opengraph-image
60: └── globals.css             # Theme tokens + utilities (panel, glass, pulse-dot, num, rise)
61: 
62: src/
63: ├── components/
64: │   ├── AppShell.tsx                # Sidebar + top bar + mobile bottom nav, "Simulate Ticket" button
65: │   └── CustomerSimulationWidget.tsx
66: ├── lib/
67: │   ├── seo.ts                      # SITE_* constants + pageMetadata() helper
68: │   └── utils.ts                    # cn() (clsx + tailwind-merge)
69: └── store/
70:     └── swapdesk.tsx                # Global demo state + SwapDeskProvider
71: ```
72: 
73: ## Demo Flow
74: 
75: Everything is driven by a client-side store — no network calls.
76: 
77: 1. Click **Simulate Ticket** (top bar) or open **Customer Simulation** (`/simulate`), type a complaint, and submit.
78: 2. The store appends a ticket with status `Agent Processing` (`INTAKE` / `ROUTING` actions).
79: 3. It appears instantly in **Mission Control** and the **Inbox**, filterable by status.
80: 4. Open any ticket to inspect its execution timeline, actions, and SKU reservation.
81: 5. **Simulate Ticket** also decrements stock for `AJ4-MIL-43` (5 → 4) — visible on `/inventory`.
82: 6. **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) clears tickets and restores stock.
83: 
84: ## State Management
85: 
86: `src/store/swapdesk.tsx` exposes a `SwapDeskProvider` (mounted in `app/layout.tsx`) plus a `useSwapDesk()` hook:
87: 
88: ```ts
89: const { tickets, inventory, simulateTicket, submitCustomerTicket, resetMockData, getTicket } =
90:   useSwapDesk();
91: ```
92: 
93: - `TicketStatus` = `"resolved" | "escalated" | "processing"`
94: - `simulateTicket(): Ticket` — prepends `TCK-9045+` resolved ticket, decrements `AJ4-MIL-43` stock.
95: - `submitCustomerTicket(message): Ticket` — prepends a `processing` ticket with your message.
96: - `resetMockData()` — wipes tickets, restores initial inventory.
97: - `getTicket(id)` — look up a single ticket.
98: 
99: ## Routes
100: 
101: | Route                 | Page                    | Type            | Notes                              |
102: | --------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------- |
103: | `/`                   | Mission Control         | server + client | metrics + live queue, filter       |
104: | `/inbox`              | Inbox                   | server          | static ticket list                 |
105: | `/inventory`          | Inventory               | server layout + client page | stock reacts to simulations |
106: | `/database`           | Database Schema         | server          |                                    |
107: | `/integrations`       | Integrations            | server layout + client page | webhook toggle + URL copy  |
108: | `/settings`           | Agent Settings          | server          |                                    |
109: | `/simulate`           | Customer Simulation     | server          | `CustomerSimulationWidget`         |
110: | `/ticket/[id]`        | Ticket Execution        | client          | Partial Prerender (Suspense)       |
111: | `/robots.txt`         | —                       | metadata route  | auto-generated                     |
112: | `/sitemap.xml`        | —                       | metadata route  | auto-generated                     |
113: | `/opengraph-image`    | —                       | image route     | generated 1200×630 PNG             |
114: | `/twitter-image`      | —                       | image route     | re-export of opengraph-image       |
115: 
116: > **Turbopack dynamic route note:** `/ticket/[id]` must pre-render its HTML shell at build time. Client hooks that need URL data (`useParams`, `usePathname`) therefore live behind `<Suspense>` and out of the static shell. See `app/ticket/[id]/page.tsx`.
117: 
118: ## Design System
119: 
120: Theme tokens live in `app/globals.css` as CSS variables and Tailwind v4 `@theme` mappings:
121: 
122: - Colors: `--card: #111113`, `--border: #222225`, `--color-success` (green), `--color-primary`, `--color-warning`, `--color-danger`, `--color-hairline`
123: - Type: `font-display` (`--font-bricolage`), `font-sans` (`--font-jakarta`), `font-mono` (`--font-geist-mono`)
124: - Utilities: `panel` (card), `glass` (frosted nav), `pulse-dot`, `num` (tabular numerals), `rise` (entry animation)
125: 
126: > **Guideline:** keep server-rendered pages static where possible and move interactivity into client components. Do not introduce a visual redesign — extend the existing token system.
127: 
128: ## SEO
129: 
130: Add full metadata to every segment:
131: 
132: - Root (`app/layout.tsx`): `metadataBase`, titles with `template: "%s · SwapDesk"`, description, keywords, `<viewport>` (themeColor), OpenGraph + Twitter cards, `robots`, `applicationName`, authors, category.
133: - Per page: use the `pageMetadata({ title, description, path })` helper from `src/lib/seo.ts` (marked `Export const metadata`).
134: - Images: `app/opengraph-image.tsx` generates a themed 1200×630 card with `ImageResponse`; `app/twitter-image.tsx` re-exports it.
135: - Crawling: `app/robots.ts` and `app/sitemap.ts` reflect the remaining routes.
136: 
137: Set the title without the site name suffix — the root template appends ` · SwapDesk`.
138: 
139: ## Deploy
140: 
141: Deploy on Vercel (or any Node host running `npm run build && npm run start`):
142: 
143: ```bash
144: npm run build
145: npm run start
146: ```
147: 
148: Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` to your production origin so canonical URLs, sitemap, and robots are correct.

2: 
3: Business outcomes (arranged/clarification/denial/escalation) are always
4: HTTP 200 with an `outcome` field: a denial is an answer, not an error.
5: HTTP errors mean transport problems only: 404 unknown case, 422 bad
6: request, 500 unexpected failure (generic message, never internals).
7: 
8: Execution is synchronous per request; the demo database makes status
9: reads available at any time. No authentication: this is a local mock,
10: and the docs say so. Demo-only failure controls live under /v1/demo
11: and never touch ordinary endpoints.

1: # SwapDesk: neatHack Build Plan
2: 
3: Prepared for the neatHack team, October 10, 2026
4: 
5: ## Overview
6: 
7: SwapDesk is a customer support agent that resolves tickets instead of only answering them. It reads a customer's message, looks up the order and the business's policy, and picks one of four outcomes: resolve the issue, ask the customer a question, deny the request under policy, or escalate to a human with a short summary. When it resolves a ticket, it takes real actions through tools, such as reserving a replacement, creating a return and making a shipping label, and it records each action with an operation ID. If a step times out or fails, it checks what already happened before it tries again, so nothing is done twice. Before it replies, it compares the saved records with what it is about to say. The policy, tools and database form a swappable setup, and an online shoe store is the one we build and demo.
8: 
9: The hackathon scores evidence of reliability more than novelty: the tools, the demo and building in public make up 60% of the score. SwapDesk is built to produce that evidence. Every test ticket has a known correct outcome, so a checker script scores each run, and the failures we inject (a label timeout, a sold-out size, a worker crash) give us a recovery run to show. We run a weak first version on about 30 test cases, read the neatlogs traces, fix what broke, and run again, which gives the before and after numbers the judges ask for. We code through OpenCode with Entire on, so each fix has a checkpoint, and we price the agent per resolved ticket in cfo.ai. The originality score will be low because customer support is a crowded category. We accept that trade for a build we can finish and prove.
10: 
11: ## How well SwapDesk fits
12: 
13: SwapDesk fits well, and it is a better version of the plain refund idea. Exchanges involve several actions that change state (reserve stock, create a return, create a label), so duplicate actions and mid-run failures are real problems and not staged ones. That is exactly what the "state" and "recovery" criteria reward. The checker design is also solid.
14: 
15: Three things to fix before building:
16: 
17: 1. Cut the scope in layers. Build exchange plus refund-or-deny first. Add the worker-restart failure last, because it is the hardest. If time runs short, drop it and keep the timeout and sold-out failures.
18: 2. Make "the explanation matches saved state" checkable. Have the agent output a structured list of the actions it claims it took, and let the checker compare that list to the database. Do not try to parse the customer reply.
19: 3. Test early that traces survive a crash. If you kill the worker mid-run, check that neatlogs still has the spans up to that point. This is unverified, so test it in the first few hours.
20: 
21: ## What the agent does
22: 
23: A customer writes, "These shoes don't fit, I need a size 43." The agent:
24: 
25: 1. Looks up the order and the return policy.
26: 2. Decides whether the request is eligible: exchange, refund, deny, or escalate to a human.
27: 3. For an exchange, finds stock, reserves the replacement, creates the return and the label, and records each step with an operation ID.
28: 4. Runs a verification step that checks the saved state against what it intends to tell the customer.
29: 5. Replies with what actually happened.
30: 
31: If a step fails, it checks the operation status before trying again. It never repeats an action blindly.
32: 
33: ## Benchmark and numbers
34: 
35: Make about 30 cases: clean exchanges, out-of-window requests, sold-out sizes, duplicate requests, vague tickets, label timeouts, and a mid-run crash.
36: 
37: Track four numbers:
38: 
39: - Completion rate on recoverable cases
40: - Duplicate-action rate
41: - Wrongful-action rate
42: - Cost per case
43: 
44: Save the baseline V1 numbers first, then V2 after the fix.
45: 
46: ## How the three tools win points
47: 
48: ### neatlogs
49: 
50: - What to do: turn it on in the first commit. Name your runs "v1 baseline" and "v2 fixed."
51: - Evidence to save: trace links for the duplicate-label failure, the recovery run, and the fixed run, plus the numbers you compared.
52: 
53: ### Entire
54: 
55: - What to do: enable it before your first commit and commit through OpenCode. Test one commit right away.
56: - Evidence to save: a screenshot of the checkpoint for the safe-retry fix.
57: 
58: ### cfo.ai
59: 
60: - What to do: sign up now, since the card step can fail. Feed it your cost per case from neatlogs.
61: - Evidence to save: the business plan file.
62: 
63: One story to build the video around: a failed trace in neatlogs, then a coding-agent session that fixes it (Entire records it), then a clean second run. neatlogs lists an MCP integration, which could let your coding agent read the trace directly. This is unconfirmed for OpenCode, so check in the first hour. If it does not work, paste the trace into the coding agent by hand.
64: 
65: For cfo.ai, build three scenarios: base, growth, and "bad reliability," where retries and duplicates push the cost per case up. That shows reliability is your margin, which is the strongest link between the agent and the business plan. Label the $49 per store per month and $0.50 per extra case pricing as assumptions, not facts.
66: 
67: ## Order of work
68: 
69: 1. Hour 0 to 1: tool setup and a test commit.
70: 2. Hours 1 to 6: build the mock shop, then the checker, before the agent.
71: 3. Hours 6 to 10: V1 agent and the baseline run.
72: 4. Hours 10 to 24: add the failures, read traces, fix, and rerun.
73: 5. Day 2: cfo.ai plan, a simple screen showing a live run, and repo cleanup.
74: 6. Oct 12 afternoon: record the video, with plenty of time before submission opens at 7 PM IST.
75: 
76: Post on X with #neatHack at about hours 1, 6, 14, 24 and 40. Each post should show a trace or a checker result.
77: 
78: ## What to watch
79: 
80: - The demo plan covers 1:40 of agent behavior. The 3-minute video must also explicitly cover neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai, so plan about 1:20 for the tools.
81: - If the agent passes everything on run 1, there is no before/after story. Make a few cases hard enough to fail.
82: - The originality score will be low. The edge is execution evidence, and that is what the time allows.
83: 
84: ## PRD: Problem, goals and scope
85: 
86: **Problem.** Support staff spend their time coordinating order history, return policies, inventory and shipping to finish one request. Agents that only chat leave that work undone, and agents that act can double-charge, double-ship or claim success they did not achieve. A customer support agent is only useful if it finishes the job correctly and knows when to stop.
87: 
88: **Product.** SwapDesk is a customer support resolution agent. The core agent is general. The business setup (policy document, tool definitions, database) is swappable. The demo setup is a fictional online shoe store.
89: 
90: **Goals**
91: 
92: 1. Resolve eligible tickets end to end with correct state in the database.
93: 2. Recover from tool failures without repeating any committed action.
94: 3. Escalate or ask when it cannot safely resolve, and say so honestly.
95: 4. Produce measurable before and after results, a recovery run, traces, checkpoints and a business plan, as the judges require.
96: 
97: **Non-goals**
98: 
99: - Real payments, real shipping or real customer data.
100: - A polished chatbot experience. The completed transaction is the product.
101: - Working for any business. We claim it works on the shoe store and is built so tools and policies can be swapped.
102: - A second store, unless the first one is finished early. A small second setup with about 5 tickets is a stretch goal only.
103: 
104: **Users**
105: 
106: - Shop customers, who write a ticket in plain language.
107: - Support staff, who receive escalations with a summary and can see what the agent did.
108: 
109: **Scope for v1**
110: 
111: - One item per request.
112: - Request types: exchange, refund eligibility, and escalation. Refunds and exchanges are simulated.
113: - Mock services: orders, sizes and inventory, return rules, shipping labels.
114: 
115: ## PRD: Agent behavior
116: 
117: **Workflow**
118: 
119: 1. Read the ticket and identify the order and item.
120: 2. Fetch the order and the return policy.
121: 3. Decide the outcome: resolve, ask the customer, deny, or escalate.
122: 4. For an exchange, find stock, reserve the replacement, create the return and create the label. Each action gets an operation ID.
123: 5. Verify: compare saved state with the planned reply.
124: 6. Reply with what actually happened.
125: 
126: **Outcome rules**
127: 
128: - **Resolve** only when the request is within policy and every action is confirmed in saved state.
129: - **Ask** when the ticket is too vague to act on, such as a missing size or unclear order.
130: - **Deny** when the request is outside policy, with no action taken and a clear reason given.
131: - **Escalate** when the agent cannot complete or verify the action, with a short summary for a human.
132: 
133: **Tools**
134: 
135: - `get_order`, `get_return_policy`
136: - `find_exchange_stock`, `reserve_replacement`
137: - `create_return`, `create_label`
138: - `get_operation_status`, `verify_exchange`
139: 
140: **Failure handling requirements**
141: 
142: 1. If `create_label` succeeds but the response times out, the agent calls `get_operation_status` and does not create a second label.
143: 2. If the requested size sells out before reservation, the agent rereads stock and offers an allowed alternative. It never changes the size silently.
144: 3. If the worker stops after a reservation, a restart resumes from saved progress and does not reserve twice. This is built last and dropped first if time runs short.
145: 4. Retries are bounded. After the limit, the agent escalates.
146: 
147: ## PRD: Verification and metrics
148: 
149: A separate checker script, not the agent, decides whether a run passed. It reads the final database state and asserts:
150: 
151: - The correct order and item were handled, and the request was within policy.
152: - The replacement size matches the customer's request.
153: - Exactly one reservation, one return and one label exist for an exchange.
154: - Inventory never goes negative.
155: - The agent's list of claimed actions matches the saved state. The agent outputs that list in a structured form so the checker does not have to read the customer reply.
156: - An ineligible request caused no action.
157: 
158: The test set is about 30 tickets: clean exchanges, out-of-window requests, sold-out sizes, duplicate requests, vague tickets, label timeouts and a mid-run crash. Several must be hard enough that a simple first version fails them.
159: 
160: | Metric | Definition | Why it matters |
161: |---|---|---|
162: | Completion rate | Share of recoverable cases ending in the correct final state | Main agent score |
163: | Duplicate-action rate | Share of runs with more than one reservation, return or label | Safety under retries |
164: | Wrongful-action rate | Share of ineligible requests where the agent took an action | Safety under policy |
165: | False-resolution rate | Share of runs where the agent says resolved but the checker disagrees | Trust when unwatched |
166: | Cost per case | Model and tool cost per ticket from neatlogs | Feeds the cfo.ai plan |
167: 
168: Record V1 and V2 numbers from real runs. No target is set in advance, and nothing is reported that the runs did not produce.
169: 
170: ## PRD: Sponsor tool requirements
171: 
172: - **neatlogs:** on from the first commit. Runs are named "v1 baseline" and "v2 fixed." We save trace links for the duplicate-label failure, the recovery run and the fixed run, with the numbers compared.
173: - **Entire:** enabled before the first commit, with all commits made through OpenCode. We save a screenshot of the checkpoint for the safe-retry fix.
174: - **cfo.ai:** signed up early because the card step can fail. We model stores times subscription price, case volume times cost per case, support costs and runway, in three scenarios: base, growth and bad reliability. The business plan file goes in the submission.
175: - **Public evidence:** a public repo with commits dated during the event, and posts on X tagged #neatHack with a trace or checker result in each.
176: 
177: ## PRD: Business assumptions
178: 
179: These are assumptions to test in cfo.ai, not facts.
180: 
181: - Price: $49 per store per month including 100 resolved cases, then $0.50 per extra case.
182: - Cost drivers: model tokens per case, retries, hosting and database, merchant onboarding and support.
183: - Shipping and refunds are merchant expenses. They are not our revenue or our software cost.
184: - Reliability is the margin: more retries and duplicates raise the cost per case, which the bad-reliability scenario shows.
185: 
186: ## PRD: Risks and open questions
187: 
188: - **Chatbot risk:** the agent becomes a chatbot with decorative tools. The checker must judge the database, not the wording of the reply.
189: - **No before/after story:** if V1 passes everything, there is nothing to improve. Seed hard cases.
190: - **Originality:** low, since customer support is crowded. We rely on execution evidence.
191: - **Unverified:** whether neatlogs keeps spans when the worker crashes, and whether OpenCode can connect to the neatlogs MCP. Both are tested in the first hours.
192: - **Video time:** the 3-minute video must cover neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai explicitly, so about 1:20 goes to the tools.
193: - **Open question:** which model runs the agent, and what cost per case that implies.

189:                             f"(only {available} unit(s) in stock); reply "
190:                             "with an alternative size or ask for a human",
191:                 "attempts": log_attempts}
192: 
193:     def _key(step: str) -> str:
194:         return f"{case_id}:{run_id}:{step}"
195: 
196:     try:
197:         res = _attempt(log_attempts, "reserve", lambda: reserve_replacement(
198:             db_path, case_id=case_id, run_id=run_id,
199:             op_key=_key("reserve"), order_id=order_id,
200:             order_item_id=order_item_id, size=authorized, qty=qty,
201:             requested_size=size, consent=authorized != size))
202:     except _Exhausted as exc:
203:         return {**_escalate_none(
204:             db_path, case_id, f"reservation kept failing: {exc}"),
205:             "attempts": log_attempts}
206:     except OperationError as exc:
207:         return {**_escalate_none(db_path, case_id, f"reservation failed: {exc}"),
208:                 "attempts": log_attempts}
209:     if res.duplicate and res.status == "arranged":
210:         return {"outcome": "arranged", "exchange_id": res.exchange_id,
211:                 "duplicate": True, "attempts": log_attempts}
212:     exchange_id = res.exchange_id
213: 
214:     def _do_return():
215:         return create_return(db_path, case_id=case_id, run_id=run_id,
216:                              op_key=_key("return"), exchange_id=exchange_id)
217: 
218:     def _do_label():
219:         return create_label(db_path, case_id=case_id, run_id=run_id,
220:                             op_key=_key("label"), exchange_id=exchange_id)
221: 
222:     def _do_finalize():
223:         return finalize_arranged(
224:             db_path, case_id=case_id, run_id=run_id,
225:             op_key=_key("finalize"), exchange_id=exchange_id)
226: 
227:     try:
228:         _attempt(log_attempts, "return", _do_return)
229:         _attempt(log_attempts, "label", _do_label)
230:         _attempt(log_attempts, "finalize", _do_finalize)
231:     except _Exhausted as exc:
232:         return {**_escalate_held(db_path, case_id, run_id, exchange_id,
233:                                  f"flow kept failing: {exc}", log_attempts),
234:                 "attempts": log_attempts}
235:     except OperationError as exc:
236:         return {**_escalate_held(db_path, case_id, run_id, exchange_id,
237:                                  f"flow failed: {exc}", log_attempts),
238:                 "attempts": log_attempts}
239:     return {"outcome": "arranged", "exchange_id": exchange_id,

1: """Agent orchestration: one tool-using loop, bounded and resumable.
2: 
3: One concern only: running a case. The model chooses tools from observed
4: results; the outcome and the customer reply are derived from database
5: state afterwards, never from model prose. Orchestration checkpoints
6: (LangGraph threads) are separate from business-action records: resuming
7: reuses the same tool keys, so backend idempotency still governs effects.
8: """
9: 
10: from __future__ import annotations
11: 
12: import json
13: import os
14: import sqlite3
15: from contextlib import contextmanager
16: from dataclasses import dataclass
17: from pathlib import Path
18: 
19: import neatlogs
20: 
21: from .. import telemetry
22: from ..operations import get_case, verify_exchange
23: from .prompts import (
24:     OUTCOME_ARRANGED,
25:     OUTCOME_CLARIFICATION,
26:     OUTCOME_DENIAL,
27:     OUTCOME_ESCALATION,
28:     SYSTEM_PROMPT,
29:     render_reply,
30: )
31: from .tools import ToolContext, build_tools
32: 
33: DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS = 12
34: 
35: 
36: class ConfigurationError(Exception):
37:     """Agent misconfiguration (e.g. no model selected)."""
38: 
39: 
40: @dataclass(frozen=True)
41: class AgentContext:
42:     db_path: str | Path
43:     case_id: str
44:     run_id: str
45:     message: str
46:     consent_size: str | None = None
47: 
48: 
49: # User-specified direct-Gemini model. Override with SWAPDESK_MODEL.
50: DEFAULT_MODEL_ID = "gemini-3.8-flash"
51: 
52: # Hackathon LiteLLM proxy (OpenAI-compatible). Override with LITELLM_BASE_URL.
53: LITELLM_DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "https://litellm.vision.aivar.app/v1"
54: LITELLM_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID = "claude-haiku"
55: 
56: 
57: def resolve_model_id(explicit: str | None = None) -> str:
58:     """Model id: explicit arg, else SWAPDESK_MODEL, else the default."""
59:     return explicit or os.environ.get("SWAPDESK_MODEL") or DEFAULT_MODEL_ID
60: 
61: 
62: def build_model(model_id: str | None = None):
63:     """Provider chat model from environment, never hardcoded to one.
64: 
65:     LITELLM_API_KEY present → OpenAI-compatible client at the LiteLLM
66:     proxy (hackathon key). Else GEMINI_API_KEY → direct Gemini. Else a
67:     clear ConfigurationError. SDK retries are disabled on both paths:
68:     every request is exactly one attempt, so a middleware request cap
69:     means what it says.
70:     """
71:     telemetry.load_dotenv()
72:     if "LITELLM_API_KEY" in os.environ:
73:         from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
74: 
75:         return ChatOpenAI(
76:             model=model_id or os.environ.get("SWAPDESK_MODEL")
77:             or LITELLM_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID,
78:             base_url=os.environ.get("LITELLM_BASE_URL",
79:                                     LITELLM_DEFAULT_BASE_URL),
80:             api_key=os.environ["LITELLM_API_KEY"],
81:             max_retries=0)
82:     if "GEMINI_API_KEY" in os.environ:
83:         from langchain_google_genai import ChatGoogleGenerativeAI
84: 
85:         return ChatGoogleGenerativeAI(model=resolve_model_id(model_id),
86:                                       max_retries=0)
87:     raise ConfigurationError(
88:         "no model provider configured: set LITELLM_API_KEY (plus "
89:         "SWAPDESK_MODEL) or GEMINI_API_KEY; nothing was called")
90: 
91: 
92: def build_agent(ctx: AgentContext, model=None, checkpointer=None, *,
93:                 middleware=(), state_schema=None, interrupt_after=None,
94:                 telemetry_enabled=True):
95:     """Compile one agent for one case run. Checkpointer may be shared."""
96:     from langchain.agents import create_agent
97: 
98:     if telemetry_enabled:
99:         telemetry.init_telemetry()
100:     model = model or build_model()
101:     if telemetry_enabled:
102:         model = telemetry.maybe_wrap_gemini(model)
103:     tools = build_tools(ToolContext(db_path=ctx.db_path,
104:                                     case_id=ctx.case_id, run_id=ctx.run_id))
105:     return create_agent(model, tools, system_prompt=SYSTEM_PROMPT,
106:                         checkpointer=checkpointer, middleware=list(middleware),
107:                         state_schema=state_schema, interrupt_after=interrupt_after)
108: 
109: 
110: def compose_input(message: str, case_id: str, run_id: str,
111:                   consent_size: str | None = None) -> str:
112:     """Production input composition, shared by direct and Studio runs."""
113:     lines = [f"case_id: {case_id}", f"run_id: {run_id}"]
114:     if consent_size:
115:         lines.append(f"recorded customer consent: accepts size "
116:                      f"{consent_size} as a replacement")
117:     lines.append(f"customer message: {message}")
118:     return "\n".join(lines)

120: 
121: def _latest_note(case: dict | None, state: str) -> str:
122:     if not case:
123:         return ""
124:     notes = case.get("progress", {}).get("notes", [])
125:     for note in reversed(notes):
126:         if note.get("state") == state:
127:             return note.get("detail", "")
128:     return ""

131: def _case_exchange(db_path, case_id: str):
132:     conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path))
133:     conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
134:     try:
135:         return conn.execute(
136:             "SELECT * FROM exchanges WHERE case_id = ?"
137:             " ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 1",
138:             (case_id,)).fetchone()
139:     finally:
140:         conn.close()
141: 
142: 
143: def _case_exchange_or_reused(db_path, case_id: str):
144:     """This case's latest exchange, else the duplicate-reused one named
145:     by its operation records."""
146:     row = _case_exchange(db_path, case_id)
147:     if row is not None:
148:         return row
149:     conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path))
150:     conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
151:     try:
152:         op = conn.execute(
153:             "SELECT result_json FROM operations WHERE case_id = ? "
154:             "ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 1", (case_id,)).fetchone()
155:         if op is None:
156:             return None
157:         try:
158:             exchange_id = json.loads(op["result_json"]).get("exchange_id")
159:         except ValueError:
160:             return None
161:         if not exchange_id:
162:             return None
163:         return conn.execute("SELECT * FROM exchanges WHERE id = ?",
164:                             (exchange_id,)).fetchone()
165:     finally:
166:         conn.close()
167: 
168: 
169: def _escalation_reason(db_path, exchange_id: str) -> str:
170:     conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path))
171:     conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
172:     try:
173:         rows = conn.execute(
174:             "SELECT details_json FROM journal WHERE event = 'released'"
175:             " ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 25").fetchall()
176:     finally:
177:         conn.close()
178:     for row in rows:
179:         try:
180:             details = json.loads(row["details_json"])
181:         except ValueError:
182:             continue
183:         if details.get("exchange_id") == exchange_id:
184:             return details.get("reason", "")
185:     return ""
186: 
187: 
188: def derive_outcome(ctx: AgentContext) -> dict:
189:     """Decide the outcome from persisted state. The model is not asked."""
190:     case = get_case(ctx.db_path, ctx.case_id)
191:     state = case["state"] if case else None
192:     if state == "arranged":
193:         row = _case_exchange_or_reused(ctx.db_path, ctx.case_id)
194:         if row is None:
195:             return {"outcome": OUTCOME_ESCALATION, "exchange_id": None,
196:                     "data": {"reason": "arranged case has no exchange row",
197:                              "partial": "data inconsistent"}}
198:         hand = verify_exchange(ctx.db_path, row["id"])
199:         return {"outcome": OUTCOME_ARRANGED, "exchange_id": row["id"],
200:                 "data": {"exchange_id": row["id"],
201:                          "return_id": hand.return_id,
202:                          "label_id": hand.label_id,
203:                          "tracking_ref": hand.tracking_ref}}
204:     if state == "denied":
205:         return {"outcome": OUTCOME_DENIAL, "exchange_id": None,
206:                 "data": {"reason": _latest_note(case, "denied")}}
207:     if state == "needs_information":
208:         return {"outcome": OUTCOME_CLARIFICATION, "exchange_id": None,
209:                 "data": {"question": _latest_note(case, "needs_information")}}
210:     if state in ("escalated", "cleanup_pending"):
211:         row = _case_exchange(ctx.db_path, ctx.case_id)
212:         if row is None:
213:             return {"outcome": OUTCOME_ESCALATION, "exchange_id": None,
214:                     "data": {"reason": _latest_note(case, "escalated"),
215:                              "partial": "no exchange started"}}
216:         hand = verify_exchange(ctx.db_path, row["id"])
217:         partial = (f"{hand.status}, hold "
218:                    f"{'active' if hand.hold_active else 'released'}, "
219:                    f"return {hand.return_id or 'none'}, "
220:                    f"label {hand.label_id or 'none'}")
221:         return {"outcome": OUTCOME_ESCALATION, "exchange_id": row["id"],
222:                 "data": {"reason": _escalation_reason(ctx.db_path, row["id"]),
223:                          "partial": partial}}
224:     return {"outcome": OUTCOME_ESCALATION, "exchange_id": None,
225:             "data": {"reason": "agent made no progress",
226:                      "partial": f"case state {state!r}"}}
227: 
228: 
229: def run_agent(ctx: AgentContext, model=None, checkpointer=None,
230:               max_tool_calls: int = DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS) -> dict:
231:     """Run one case to a verified outcome. Bounded; flushes telemetry."""
232:     agent = build_agent(ctx, model=model, checkpointer=checkpointer)
233:     config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": ctx.run_id},
234:               "recursion_limit": 2 * max_tool_calls + 5}
235:     try:
236:         with neatlogs.trace(f"swapdesk:{ctx.case_id}",
237:                              kind="WORKFLOW") as span:
238:             span.set_attribute("swapdesk.case_id", ctx.case_id)
239:             span.set_attribute("swapdesk.run_id", ctx.run_id)
240:             span.set_attribute("swapdesk.benchmark",
241:                                telemetry.BENCHMARK_VERSION)
242:             if ctx.consent_size:
243:                 span.set_attribute("swapdesk.consent_size", ctx.consent_size)
244:             result = agent.invoke(
245:                 {"messages": [{"role": "user",
246:                                "content": compose_input(
247:                                    ctx.message, ctx.case_id, ctx.run_id,
248:                                    ctx.consent_size)}]},
249:                 config)
250:             decided = derive_outcome(ctx)
251:             reply = render_reply(decided["outcome"], decided["data"])
252:             neatlogs.log("case {case_id} -> {outcome}",
253:                          case_id=ctx.case_id, outcome=decided["outcome"])
254:             return {"outcome": decided["outcome"],
255:                     "exchange_id": decided["exchange_id"],
256:                     "reply": reply,
257:                     "messages": result["messages"],
258:                     "data": decided["data"],
259:                     "exporting": telemetry.is_exporting()}
260:     finally:
261:         telemetry.flush()
262: 
263: 
264: @contextmanager
265: def sqlite_checkpointer(path: str | Path):
266:     """File-backed LangGraph checkpointer, separate from business data."""
267:     path = Path(path)
268:     path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
269:     from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite import SqliteSaver
270: 
271:     # Same-thread check off: the graph may execute nodes on worker threads.
272:     # Still one local file, never shared between processes.
273:     conn = sqlite3.connect(str(path), check_same_thread=False)
274:     try:
275:         yield SqliteSaver(conn)
276:     finally:
277:         conn.close()

## 1. What has been done vs what is left

Verified from `hackathon.md`, `README.md`, `src/swapdesk/api.py`, `service.py`, `agent/`, `frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx`:

**Done (backend):**

- `src/swapdesk/db.py, operations.py, fixtures.py, policy.py`: atomic reserve, idempotency (same key+payload=replay, same key+different payload=reject), 30-day/final-sale policy, 1-active-exchange/item.
- `operations.py` full lifecycle: `reserve→return→label→finalize→arranged` + `release/cancel/escalate/verify`, `faults.py` injection.
- `checker.py + eval/cases_v1.json + driver.py/harness.py/run.py`: 30 frozen cases / 42 runs, deterministic checker.
- `agent/graph.py, tools.py, prompts.py, telemetry.py`: `create_agent` + 14 tools, bounded loop (`max_tool_calls=12`), file checkpointer, DB-derived outcome/reply, neatlogs spans.
- `agent/studio_flow.py + studio.py + langgraph.json`: `prepare→agent→verify` graph, two assistants: `swapdesk_offline` (scripted, zero model calls) and `swapdesk_live` (budget-capped Gemini).
- `api.py + service.py`: `POST /v1/tickets`, `GET /v1/cases/{id}`, `/timeline`, `/continue`, `/fixtures`, `/demo/faults`, `/health`. Sync execution, 200+`outcome` for `arranged/clarification/denial/escalation`.
- `docs/business/`, `EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md`, `STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`.

**Done (frontend):**

- Next.js 16 + React 19 + Tailwind v4 dashboard: `/, /inbox, /inventory, /database, /integrations, /settings, /simulate, /ticket/[id]`.
- State is 100% client mock in `frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx:84-130`: `simulateTicket()`, `submitCustomerTicket()` just prepend to `useState`, decrement `AJ4-MIL-43`. No `fetch`, no `EventSource`.

**Left / gaps (`hackathon.md:192-200`):**

1. **No wiring:** `api.py:142` calls `service.submit_ticket()->_run_flow()` (deterministic rules), never `agent/graph.py:229 run_agent()` nor `studio_flow.py:357 build_offline_graph()`. Frontend never calls API.
2. No live agent execution visible in UI.
3. No 42-run re-baseline, no recovery/crash live coverage, `live_graph` unverified, license, video/X-post/submission packaging.

## 2. How to connect LangGraph → FastAPI → frontend

Current split:

```
frontend (mock store)  X  FastAPI (service._run_flow)  X  LangGraph (studio_flow graphs in studio_data/)
```

You need:

```
Next.js --SSE/poll--> FastAPI --astream--> LangGraph graph --tools--> SQLite (swapdesk.db)
```

### Backend: add streaming endpoint

1. Add CORS in `src/swapdesk/api.py:123` for `localhost:3000`:
```python
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=["http://localhost:3000"], allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"])
```

2. Don't reuse served `studio.py:23 offline_graph` directly — it's compiled without checkpointer (platform provides it). In FastAPI you must compile with one:
```python
from swapdesk.agent.studio_flow import build_offline_graph
from swapdesk.agent.graph import sqlite_checkpointer
```

3. New route `POST /v1/tickets/stream` returning `StreamingResponse(text/event-stream)`:
```python
async def event_gen():
  with sqlite_checkpointer(".langgraph_api/checkpoints.db") as cp:
    graph = build_offline_graph(checkpointer=cp)
    async for chunk in graph.astream(
      {"scenario":"arrange","message":body.message,...},
      config={"configurable":{"thread_id":run_id}},
      stream_mode=["messages","updates"]):
      # map: AIMessage.tool_calls -> {"type":"tool_call","name","args"}
      # map: ToolMessage -> {"type":"tool_result","name","ok"}
      # map: verify node -> {"type":"terminal","outcome","reply","exchange_id"}
      yield f"data: {json.dumps(evt)}\n\n"
```
Use `offline` mode for keyless demo; gate `live` behind `SWAPDESK_MODEL+GEMINI_API_KEY` via `_require_live_config()` in `studio_flow.py:87`.

4. Keep existing `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline` (`api.py:162`) as fallback poll — it already returns journal+ops sanitized by `service.case_timeline()`.

5. Unify DB: decide `swapdesk.db` (shared, `service.default_db_path()`) vs `studio_data/{case}/shop.db` (`studio_flow.py:73 _case_db`). For frontend demo use shared DB, pass `db_path` through.

### Frontend: replace mock store with API client

1. Add `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`:
```ts
export const API = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SWAPDESK_API_URL ?? "http://127.0.0.1:8000";
```

2. In `frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx:89,102` replace `simulateTicket/submitCustomerTicket` internals with:
```ts
const es = new EventSource(`${API}/v1/tickets/stream?...`);
es.onmessage = (m) => { const e = JSON.parse(m.data); /* append to actions: RESERVE_STOCK, CREATE_LABEL... */ };
```
Render `processing → resolved/escalated` incrementally. Keep mock as fallback when `!API`.

3. `app/ticket/[id]/page.tsx`: on mount, `fetch GET /v1/cases/{id}` + `/timeline`, plus subscribe to stream for live steps. Reuse existing `actions[]` UI — just feed it real `op_key/op_type/event` from `TimelineEvent` (`api.py:78`).

Fastest demo without new code today: `POST /v1/tickets` then poll `GET /timeline` — shows committed steps, but not live model thinking. For live thinking you need the SSE endpoint above.

Want me to implement the SSE endpoint + `lib/api.ts` wiring?

Implement the missing FastAPI → LangGraph integration.
This is execution plumbing, not another benchmark or prompt-tuning task.

First inspect current local changes and project instructions.
Preserve teammate work. Work in a focused branch through Entire.

Current problem:
POST /v1/tickets calls deterministic service._run_flow, not run_agent.
Make the normal customer path execute the existing real LangGraph agent.
Keep deterministic execution as an explicitly labeled test adapter only.
Never silently fall back to scripted execution when model configuration fails.

Publish the frontend contract FIRST, then implement it:

1. Preserve existing /v1 route names where practical.
   POST /v1/tickets saves a request and returns 202 with case_id, run_id
   and execution_status. Do not claim completion on acceptance.
   Customer message is required; order/item/size can be missing so the
   agent can ask for information. Compose supplied fields as request data,
   not hidden instructions or fabricated consent.

2. Use a minimal durable SQLite work queue and one worker.
   Save requests before execution; atomically claim work and prevent
   concurrent processing of the same case.
   Add submission idempotency: same key/payload returns the existing case;
   same key/different payload conflicts.
   Do not automatically replay interrupted mutations blindly on startup.

3. Worker invokes the existing agent, tools and verification logic.
   Reuse existing budget middleware where appropriate.
   Enforce actual provider-request limits, not just graph recursion limits.
   Use globally unique checkpoint/thread identities scoped to the case.
   Preserve recorded consent and action keys on continuation.

4. Status and timeline reads remain responsive and read-only.
   Distinguish queued/running/waiting/completed/failed execution state
   from arranged/clarification/denial/escalation business outcome.
   Return factual reply, clarification, action references, cleanup status
   and captured trace identity when available.
   Missing trace evidence stays missing; no invented links.

5. Clarification continues the existing case with validated new input.
   Terminal status reads and duplicate submissions must not start a new
   exchange. Do not expose private reasoning or credentials in events.

6. Disable /v1/demo/faults by default.
   Enable only in explicit local developer/test mode.
   Customer execution must never depend on a demo-only endpoint.
   Configure development CORS for the actual frontend origin.

7. Add deterministic HTTP-to-agent integration tests using an injected
   scripted model. These test the same execution path without paid calls.
   Cover exchange, denial, clarification/continuation, duplicate submission,
   timeout recovery and configuration/budget failure.
   Verify saved state and no duplicate actions; do not weaken the checker.

Deliver:
- Final OpenAPI contract and example request/status/timeline JSON.
- Exact API and worker startup commands.
- Test results and remaining limitations.
- Focused commit with verified Entire linkage; clean working tree.
No push, deployment, full benchmark or paid runs without approval.
Wiring the live LangGraph agent behind FastAPI — starting with the current state and contracts.

221:             {"state": state, "detail": note, "at": _db.utcnow()})
222:     now = _db.utcnow()
223:     conn.execute(
224:         """INSERT INTO cases (case_id, state, progress_json, updated_at)
225:            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
226:            ON CONFLICT(case_id) DO UPDATE SET state = excluded.state,
227:              progress_json = excluded.progress_json,
228:              updated_at = excluded.updated_at""",
229:         (case_id, state, json.dumps(progress, sort_keys=True), now),
230:     )

251: def _record_duplicate(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, op_key: str, case_id: str,
252:                       run_id: str, op_type: str, digest: str, payload: dict,
253:                       exchange: ExchangeRecord) -> dict:
254:     """Reuse an existing exchange without any new stock effect."""
255:     result = {"exchange_id": exchange.id, "status": exchange.status,
256:               "duplicate": True}
257:     _record_op(conn, op_key=op_key, case_id=case_id, run_id=run_id,
258:                op_type=op_type, digest=digest, payload=payload,
259:                status="duplicate", result=result)
260:     _journal(conn, op_key, "duplicate_reused",
261:              {"exchange_id": exchange.id,
262:               "order_item_id": exchange.order_item_id})
263:     _touch_case(conn, case_id, exchange.status)
264:     return result

267: def _transition(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, exchange_id: str, to_status: str,
268:                 op_key: str, event: str, extra: dict | None = None,
269:                 case_step: str | None = None) -> ExchangeRecord:
270:     """Move an exchange one legal step; raises IllegalTransitionError."""
271:     current = _require_exchange(conn, exchange_id)
272:     allowed = EXCHANGE_TRANSITIONS.get(current.status, frozenset())
273:     if to_status not in allowed:
274:         raise IllegalTransitionError(
275:             f"cannot move exchange {exchange_id!r} from {current.status!r} "
276:             f"to {to_status!r}; re-query status and continue from the "
277:             "persisted state")
278:     now = _db.utcnow()
279:     conn.execute("UPDATE exchanges SET status = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?",
280:                  (to_status, now, exchange_id))
281:     _touch_case(conn, current.case_id, to_status, step=case_step)
282:     details = {"exchange_id": exchange_id, "from": current.status,
283:                "to": to_status}
284:     details.update(extra or {})
285:     _journal(conn, op_key, event, details)
286:     return _require_exchange(conn, exchange_id)

289: def reserve_replacement(db_path: str | Path, *, case_id: str, run_id: str,
290:                         op_key: str, order_id: str, order_item_id: str,
291:                         size: str, qty: int = 1,
292:                         requested_size: str | None = None,
293:                         consent: bool = False) -> ReservationResult:
294:     """Reserve one replacement unit of the exact requested size.
295: 
296:     `size` is the authorized size (never substituted silently);
297:     `requested_size` records what the customer originally asked for and
298:     defaults to `size`. Authorizing a different size requires explicit
299:     recorded customer consent, otherwise this raises and writes nothing.
300:     All three join the idempotency payload.
301: 
302:     Idempotent on op_key: same key plus same payload returns the saved
303:     result; same key plus different payload raises PayloadMismatchError.
304:     A different key for an item that already has an active exchange
305:     returns the existing exchange as a duplicate without new writes.
306:     Validation failures raise and leave inventory unchanged.
307:     """
308:     if qty < 1:
309:         raise ReservationError("qty must be at least 1")
310:     if requested_size is None:
311:         requested_size = size
312:     if requested_size != size and not consent:
313:         raise ReservationError(
314:             f"size {size!r} differs from requested {requested_size!r} "
315:             "without recorded customer consent; refusing to substitute")
316:     payload = {"order_id": order_id, "order_item_id": order_item_id,
317:                "size": size, "qty": qty, "requested_size": requested_size,
318:                "consent": consent}
319:     digest = payload_hash(payload)
320:     conn = _db.connect(db_path)
321:     try:
322:         with _db.immediate(conn):
323:             saved = conn.execute(
324:                 "SELECT * FROM operations WHERE idempotency_key = ?",
325:                 (op_key,)).fetchone()
326:             if saved is not None:
327:                 if saved["payload_hash"] != digest:
328:                     raise PayloadMismatchError(
329:                         f"op_key {op_key!r} was already used with a "
330:                         "different payload")
331:                 result = json.loads(saved["result_json"])
332:                 return ReservationResult(
333:                     exchange_id=result["exchange_id"],
334:                     status=result["status"],
335:                     duplicate=result.get("duplicate", False))
336: 
337:             if _faults.consume(op_key, "transient"):
338:                 raise TransientError(
339:                     f"injected transient failure for op_key {op_key!r}; "
340:                     "nothing was written, retry with the same key")
341: 
342:             item_row = conn.execute(
343:                 "SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE id = ?", (order_item_id,)
344:             ).fetchone()
345:             if item_row is None or item_row["order_id"] != order_id:
346:                 raise ItemNotFoundError(
347:                     f"item {order_item_id!r} not found on order {order_id!r}")
348:             item = _row_to_item(item_row)
349: 
350:             eligible, reason = check_eligibility(item, date.today())
351:             if not eligible:
352:                 raise IneligibleError(reason)
353: 
354:             existing = get_active_exchange(conn, order_item_id)
355:             if existing is not None:
356:                 dup = _record_duplicate(
357:                     conn, op_key=op_key, case_id=case_id, run_id=run_id,
358:                     op_type=OP_RESERVE, digest=digest, payload=payload,
359:                     exchange=existing)
360:                 return ReservationResult(exchange_id=dup["exchange_id"],
361:                                          status=dup["status"], duplicate=True)
362: 
363:             latest = _latest_exchange(conn, order_item_id)
364:             if latest is not None and latest.status in ("arranged",
365:                                                         "escalated"):
366:                 # A finished exchange stays the answer: reuse it with no new
367:                 # stock effect. Cancelled/denied rows allow a fresh attempt.
368:                 dup = _record_duplicate(
369:                     conn, op_key=op_key, case_id=case_id, run_id=run_id,
370:                     op_type=OP_RESERVE, digest=digest, payload=payload,
371:                     exchange=latest)
372:                 return ReservationResult(exchange_id=dup["exchange_id"],
373:                                          status=dup["status"], duplicate=True)
374: 
375:             stock = conn.execute(
376:                 "SELECT * FROM stock WHERE sku = ? AND size = ?",
377:                 (item.sku, size)).fetchone()
378:             available = (stock["on_hand"] - stock["held"]
379:                          if stock is not None else 0)
380:             if _faults.consume(op_key, "deplete_stock"):
381:                 # Simulate the pool draining between lookup and write. The
382:                 # depletion rolls back with this failed transaction.
383:                 conn.execute(
384:                     "UPDATE stock SET on_hand = held WHERE sku = ? AND size = ?",
385:                     (item.sku, size))
386:                 available = 0
387:             if stock is None or available < qty:
388:                 raise InsufficientStockError(
389:                     f"only {available} unit(s) of {item.sku} size {size} "
390:                     "available; the requested size is never substituted")
391: 
392:             count = conn.execute(
393:                 "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM exchanges WHERE order_item_id = ?",
394:                 (order_item_id,)).fetchone()["n"]
395:             exchange_id = f"EXC-{order_item_id}-{count + 1}"
396:             now = _db.utcnow()
397:             conn.execute(
398:                 """INSERT INTO exchanges
399:                    (id, case_id, order_id, order_item_id, requested_size,
400:                     authorized_size, qty, status, created_at, updated_at)
401:                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
402:                 (exchange_id, case_id, order_id, order_item_id,
403:                  requested_size, size, qty, "replacement_reserved", now, now),
404:             )
405:             conn.execute(
406:                 "UPDATE stock SET held = held + ? WHERE sku = ? AND size = ?",
407:                 (qty, item.sku, size),
408:             )
409:             result = {"exchange_id": exchange_id,
410:                       "status": "replacement_reserved", "duplicate": False}
411:             conn.execute(
412:                 """INSERT INTO operations
413:                    (idempotency_key, case_id, run_id, op_type, payload_hash,
414:                     payload_json, status, result_json, created_at, updated_at)
415:                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
416:                 (op_key, case_id, run_id, OP_RESERVE, digest,
417:                  json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True), "committed",
418:                  json.dumps(result), now, now),
419:             )
420:             _journal(conn, op_key, "reserved",
421:                      {"exchange_id": exchange_id,
422:                       "order_item_id": order_item_id,
423:                       "sku": item.sku, "size": size, "qty": qty,
424:                       "requested_size": requested_size})
425:             _touch_case(conn, case_id, "replacement_reserved",
426:                         step="reserved",
427:                         note=(f"consent:{size}"
428:                               if requested_size != size and consent
429:                               else None))
430:             fresh = ReservationResult(exchange_id=exchange_id,
431:                                       status="replacement_reserved",
432:                                       duplicate=False)
433:         if _faults.consume(op_key, "crash"):
434:             # The transaction above already committed: the caller sees a
435:             # crash, but get_operation_status(op_key) reports committed.
436:             raise WorkerCrashedError(
437:                 f"worker crashed after committing op_key {op_key!r}; "
438:                 "re-query status and retry with the same key")
439:         return fresh
440:     finally:
441:         conn.close()
442:

444: def get_operation_status(db_path: str | Path,
445:                          op_key: str) -> dict | None:
446:     """Return the saved operation record, or None when unknown.
447: 
448:     None means unknown, not proof of no effect. Callers must re-query;
449:     they must never assume a fresh key is safe on an uncertain write.
450:     """
451:     conn = _db.connect(db_path)
452:     try:
453:         row = conn.execute(
454:             "SELECT * FROM operations WHERE idempotency_key = ?",
455:             (op_key,)).fetchone()
456:     finally:
457:         conn.close()
458:     if row is None:
459:         return None
460:     return {"idempotency_key": row["idempotency_key"],
461:             "case_id": row["case_id"], "run_id": row["run_id"],
462:             "op_type": row["op_type"], "status": row["status"],
463:             "payload": json.loads(row["payload_json"]),
464:             "result": json.loads(row["result_json"])}
465:

467: def create_return(db_path: str | Path, *, case_id: str, run_id: str,
468:                   op_key: str, exchange_id: str) -> ReturnResult:
469:     """Create the mock return for a reserved exchange.
470: 
471:     Idempotent on op_key. A different key after the return exists is
472:     rejected: re-query status and reuse the original key.
473:     """
474:     payload = {"exchange_id": exchange_id}
475:     digest = payload_hash(payload)
476:     conn = _db.connect(db_path)
477:     try:
478:         with _db.immediate(conn):
479:             saved = _load_saved(conn, op_key, digest)
480:             if saved is not None:
481:                 result = json.loads(saved["result_json"])
482:                 return ReturnResult(
483:                     exchange_id=result["exchange_id"],
484:                     return_id=result["return_id"],
485:                     status=result["status"], duplicate=True)
486:             if _faults.consume(op_key, "transient"):
487:                 raise TransientError(
488:                     f"injected transient failure for op_key {op_key!r}; "
489:                     "nothing was written, retry with the same key")
490:             exchange = _require_exchange(conn, exchange_id)
491:             if "return_created" not in EXCHANGE_TRANSITIONS.get(
492:                     exchange.status, frozenset()):
493:                 raise IllegalTransitionError(
494:                     f"exchange {exchange_id!r} is {exchange.status!r}, "
495:                     "not reserved; re-query status instead of minting a "
496:                     "fresh key")
497:             return_id = f"RET-{exchange_id}"
498:             now = _db.utcnow()
499:             conn.execute(
500:                 """INSERT INTO returns
501:                    (id, exchange_id, case_id, order_item_id, created_at)
502:                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
503:                 (return_id, exchange_id, exchange.case_id,
504:                  exchange.order_item_id, now),
505:             )
506:             _transition(conn, exchange_id=exchange_id,
507:                         to_status="return_created", op_key=op_key,
508:                         event="return_created",
509:                         extra={"return_id": return_id}, case_step="returned")
510:             result = {"exchange_id": exchange_id, "return_id": return_id,
511:                       "status": "return_created", "duplicate": False}
512:             _record_op(conn, op_key=op_key, case_id=case_id, run_id=run_id,
513:                        op_type=OP_RETURN, digest=digest, payload=payload,
514:                        status="committed", result=result)
515:             return ReturnResult(exchange_id=exchange_id, return_id=return_id,
516:                                 status="return_created", duplicate=False)
517:     finally:
518:         conn.close()
519:

521: def create_label(db_path: str | Path, *, case_id: str, run_id: str,
522:                  op_key: str, exchange_id: str) -> LabelResult:
523:     """Create the mock shipping label for a returned exchange.
524: 
525:     Idempotent on op_key. An armed "timeout" fault commits the label and
526:     then raises: the caller must re-query status and retry the same key.
527:     """
528:     payload = {"exchange_id": exchange_id}
529:     digest = payload_hash(payload)
530:     conn = _db.connect(db_path)
531:     try:
532:         with _db.immediate(conn):
533:             saved = _load_saved(conn, op_key, digest)
534:             if saved is not None:
535:                 result = json.loads(saved["result_json"])
536:                 return LabelResult(
537:                     exchange_id=result["exchange_id"],
538:                     label_id=result["label_id"],
539:                     tracking_ref=result["tracking_ref"],
540:                     status=result["status"], duplicate=True)
541:             if _faults.consume(op_key, "transient"):
542:                 raise TransientError(
543:                     f"injected transient failure for op_key {op_key!r}; "
544:                     "nothing was written, retry with the same key")
545:             exchange = _require_exchange(conn, exchange_id)
546:             if "label_created" not in EXCHANGE_TRANSITIONS.get(
547:                     exchange.status, frozenset()):
548:                 raise IllegalTransitionError(
549:                     f"exchange {exchange_id!r} is {exchange.status!r}, "
550:                     "not return_created; re-query status instead of minting "
551:                     "a fresh key")
552:             label_id = f"LBL-{exchange_id}"
553:             tracking_ref = f"TRK-MOCK-{exchange_id}"
554:             now = _db.utcnow()
555:             ret = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM returns WHERE exchange_id = ?",
556:                                (exchange_id,)).fetchone()
557:             if ret is None:
558:                 raise OperationError(
559:                     f"exchange {exchange_id!r} is return_created but has no "
560:                     "return row; data is inconsistent, refusing to label")
561:             conn.execute(
562:                 """INSERT INTO labels (id, return_id, exchange_id,
563:                    tracking_ref, created_at)
564:                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
565:                 (label_id, ret["id"], exchange_id, tracking_ref, now),
566:             )
567:             _transition(conn, exchange_id=exchange_id,
568:                         to_status="label_created", op_key=op_key,
569:                         event="label_created",
570:                         extra={"label_id": label_id,
571:                                "tracking_ref": tracking_ref},
572:                         case_step="labeled")
573:             result = {"exchange_id": exchange_id, "label_id": label_id,
574:                       "tracking_ref": tracking_ref,
575:                       "status": "label_created", "duplicate": False}
576:             _record_op(conn, op_key=op_key, case_id=case_id, run_id=run_id,
577:                        op_type=OP_LABEL, digest=digest, payload=payload,
578:                        status="committed", result=result)
579:             out = LabelResult(exchange_id=exchange_id, label_id=label_id,
580:                               tracking_ref=tracking_ref,
581:                               status="label_created", duplicate=False)
582:         if _faults.consume(op_key, "timeout"):
583:             # The label above already committed: the response is lost, not
584:             # the effect. Same key to recover; exactly one label exists.
585:             raise LabelTimeoutError(
586:                 f"label response timed out for op_key {op_key!r} after "
587:                 "commit; re-query status and retry with the same key")
588:         return out
589:     finally:
590:         conn.close()
591:
